prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its active peptide form, which made incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: Round 1 left one real question: who takes the third place in B042, and is the citation about discovery or about drug development. I have reassessed it and still prefer Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. A prize recognises a specific discovery that changed a field, and here that discovery is the identification of GLP-1 as an incretin and satiety signal derived from proglucagon, the active GLP-1(7-36) form and its insulinotropic action in humans, and the receptor and tissue biology that followed. Holst, Mojsov and Drucker map onto those three steps without overlap. The maturity is not in question: decades of independent confirmation, several approved agents, and randomized outcome trials in glycaemia, weight, cardiovascular and renal disease. A citation that names the active peptide form and says it made incretin-based treatment possible lets the clinical consequence be stated without spending a laureate slot on it. I remain with a single-part prize because a second part would force a name out of a part whose attribution is already tight, and nothing in round 1 showed that a second achievement is stronger than the cost of that cut.
statement.case_against: The attribution weakness is unchanged and I cannot remove it from the supplied files. Knudsen's work on durable, albumin-binding long-acting analogues is what reached patients, and a discovery trio can be read as honouring the biology while leaving out the drug. Mojsov's priority relative to Habener and others is described as contested by every member, including me, and none of us has verified it. If the committee decides that therapy development is the centre of the story, my configuration is the wrong one and El-Manira's is the better answer. A separate risk is that I am treating protein engineering as less original than it was: turning a peptide with a half-life of minutes into a once-weekly drug required real chemical insight, not routine optimisation, and I may be drawing the discovery line more narrowly than the Nobel tradition does.

responses.point: El-Manira keeps Knudsen as the third name with a citation covering discovery of GLP-1 physiology and development of long-acting therapies, and says he would accept Mojsov in her place if the peptide-identification record proves firmer than he can verify.
responses.response: I have taken the Knudsen case seriously and I stay where I was, but for a narrower reason than in round 1. The chair has pointed out that neither of us can settle Mojsov's priority from the supplied files. That cuts in both directions, so it does not by itself favour Knudsen. What decides it for me is the structure of the credit. Holst and Drucker already cover physiology and receptor biology, and the active-peptide step is a distinct discovery that no other name on the list covers. Knudsen's contribution is real and I would not call it routine, but it follows from the earlier discovery and I think the citation can carry it. I would be happy to hear a concrete argument that the committee cannot defend Mojsov's inclusion, and if that appeared I would move to Knudsen rather than to a four-name or no-name outcome. Your willingness to swap shows our difference is narrow, and I would like the final vote to reflect that rather than hide it.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius raises a two-part prize pairing B042 with B033, for example Holst and Drucker with Walter, leaving Mori out, and treats the UPR as a clean basic-science discovery whose therapeutic payoff is still emerging.
responses.response: I considered this configuration seriously since it is the one the chair's third question asks about. I do not support it. Dropping Mojsov or Knudsen to make room for Walter in B042 trades a defensible GLP-1 attribution for an indefensible UPR one, because Mori and Walter independently defined the pathway and a prize that omits Mori is simply a worse B033. B033 is the cleanest credit on the shortlist and its fundamental mechanism claim is strong, which is why I keep it as my first alternative. The weaker clinical payoff does not disqualify a basic-science prize, and I agree with you on that. But it does mean there is no urgency that justifies breaking B042 to fit it in. If the committee fails to reach a defensible B042 allocation, I would vote for B033 as a stand-alone part rather than as a compromise second slot.

responses.point: Svenningsson, as chair, flags open mechanistic and safety questions for the obesity indication and asks whether discovery-centred or therapy-inclusive framing should decide the third name.
responses.response: On framing, my answer to the chair's second question is that the framing should follow the achievement, not the other way round: the shortlisted achievement is the discovery of GLP-1 physiology and its therapeutic exploitation, and a citation can say so while crediting discoverers. On the obesity safety points, I take them as valid but not as a maturity argument against B042. Questions about central mechanisms and long-term safety are normal for a drug class in wide use, and the diabetes, cardiovascular and renal evidence stands on its own. I would not want the obesity indication left unmentioned in the citation, since it is part of the clinical consequence, but I would not want the citation to claim more about mechanism than we know. This is the place where I would take your caution into the wording rather than into the configuration.

responses.point: Sandberg describes B033 as the cleanest fallback, a compact Mori and Walter pair with weaker direct clinical payoff, and keeps B042 as Drucker, Holst and Mojsov because it best fits a discovery prize.
responses.response: We agree on both the configuration and the fallback, so I will say what I think rests on that agreement. It rests on a shared view of what counts as a discovery and not on the six-way tie from the opening, and that view is exactly the point that El-Manira is contesting. I would therefore not treat five against one as strong evidence. The better test is whether the attribution would hold if challenged: the Mojsov question is the weak link and we have all flagged it. Where I would push you slightly is on B049 as a second alternative. You and Linnarsson list it, but I still think Eshhar's absence makes any CAR-T trio or pair hard to defend, so I keep B045 behind B033 only as an alternative ballot ID and do not regard either as prize-ready this year.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1 peptide can be defended as a decisive discovery credit against Habener and others, which I cannot settle from the supplied files.
Whether the committee reads the discovery line narrowly, as I do, or wide enough to include the engineering of long-acting analogues, which would favour Knudsen.
Whether the obesity indication should be named in the citation given open questions on central mechanisms and long-term safety.
Whether B045 is a better alternative ballot ID than B049, given that both have serious attribution problems.
statement.conflict_note: Unchanged from round 1. I have documented co-authorship with Per Svenningsson (about twenty works) and one 2009 paper with Abdel El Manira; neither involves a credited person on B042 or B033 and I propose no recusal. B012 (deep brain stimulation for Parkinson's disease) is close to my own research field but is not in my configuration or alternatives. I have no documented tie to Drucker, Holst, Mojsov, Knudsen, Mori or Walter.
